newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols stabilize despite choppy spot.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols stabilize despite choppy spot.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options stabilized in U.S. trading despite continued choppy trading in the spot greenback, dealers said.
"They went up a little overnight and in early (U.S.) trading, but it's been pretty steady since then," said a trader at a Canadian bank in Toronto.

One-month dollar/mark implied volatility stood at 10.4/10.6 percent, up nearly a full point from Tuesday levels but off slightly from early European trading, when the dollar shot up to fresh 34-month highs above 1.69 marks.

The dollar slid from the highs after Bundesbank spokesman Manfred Koerber said the central bank continued to support the Group of Seven (G7) communique issued last weekend, which declared that the dollar's correction from 1995 lows was over.

Still, risk reversals, which reflect pricing differential between puts and calls, were still favoring mark puts. One-month 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversal stood at 0.3/0.6 percent skewed for mark puts.
"It shows that, despite verbal intervention by officials, the market is still bullish," an investment bank trader in New York said.
The dollar/mark volatility curve remained steeply inverted as the back end lagged the uptick in the front-end. One-year dollar/mark was up half a point to 9.3/9.6 percent.

"What's interesting is that the short-term is still much higher than the long-term," the investment bank trader said, adding that this meant the market was still anticipating the volatilite environment to stay, at least for a little longer.
But a likely slowdown in the dollar's rise due to fears of central bank intervention was also keeping pressure on the front end relative to the back end, notably in dollar/yen, traders said.

Dollar/yen volatilities were up on the day but little changed from early levels, with the curve maintaining a very slight positive slope it regained on Tuesday after weeks of inversion in the run up to the G7 meeting.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 10.4/10.6 percent, up from 9.7/9.9 late on Tuesday, while six-month and one-year were up half a point to around 10.5/10.7
One-month 25-delta risk reversal stood at 0.2/0.5 percent in favor of yen puts, little changed from Tuesday.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities attracted interest as the pound soared overnight against the mark to a fresh 52-month peak of 2.7685 marks and then sharply retreated by three pfennigs.
One-month sterling/mark implied volatility stood at 10.5/10.8 percent in the U.S. afternoon, unchanged from late Tuesday but off nearly half a point from European highs.

One-month cable volatility was little changed from Tuesday at 9.5/9.8 percent as spot sterling fluctuated in relatively comfortable ranges between $1.6280 and $1.6450, well off recent peaks or bottoms against the dollar.
